verses.1:1: And it came to pass, after Israel was taken captive and Jerusalem was laid waste, that Jeremiah sat weeping, and lamented this lamentation over Jerusalem, and said: Aleph. How does the city sit solitary, she who abounded with peoples? She has become like a widow—she who was multiplied among the nations; a princess among the provinces, she has been brought under tribute.
verses.1:2: Beth. Weeping, she wept in the night, and her tears are upon her cheeks; there is none who comforts her among all who love her. All her friends have broken faith with her; they have become enemies to her.
verses.1:3: Gimel. Judea has been carried into exile because of her affliction and because of the multitude of her servitude. She dwelt among the nations; she did not find rest. All who pursued her overtook her in the midst of the oppressors.
verses.1:4: Daleth. The ways of Zion mourn, because there are none who come at the feast; all her gates are laid waste, her priests groan, her virgins are led away, and she herself is embittered within herself.
verses.1:5: He. Those who afflict her have become the head, and her enemies prospered, because the Lord humbled her for the multitude of her ungodly deeds; her little children went into captivity before the face of the oppressor.
verses.1:6: Vav. And all her beauty has been taken away from the daughter of Zion; her princes have become like rams finding no pasture, and they walked without strength before the face of the pursuer.
verses.1:7: Zayin. Jerusalem remembered the days of her humiliation and her rejections, all her desirable things that were from the days of old, when her people fell into the hands of the oppressor, and there was none who helped her. Seeing this, her enemies laughed at her habitation.
verses.1:8: Heth. Jerusalem has sinned a sin; therefore she has come into turmoil. All who glorified her have humbled her, for they saw her unseemliness; indeed, she herself groans and has turned backward.
verses.1:9: Teth. Her uncleanness is at her feet; she did not remember her latter end, and she brought down her lofty things; there is none who comforts her. Behold, O Lord, my affliction, for the enemy has magnified himself.
verses.1:10: Yod. The oppressor has stretched out his hand over all her desirable things; for she saw the nations entering into her sanctuary, concerning whom You commanded that they should not enter into Your assembly.
verses.1:11: Kaph. All her people groan, seeking bread; they have given her desirable things for food to restore the soul. Behold, O Lord, and look, for she has become dishonored.
verses.1:12: Lamed. To you, all who pass by the way, turn and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow which has come to pass; having spoken against me, the Lord has humbled me in the day of the wrath of His anger.
verses.1:13: Mem. From His height He sent fire; into my bones He brought it down. He spread a net for my feet; He turned me backward; He made me desolate, grieving in pain all the day.
verses.1:14: Nun. Watch was kept over my ungodly deeds; in my hands they were intertwined; they came up upon my neck. My strength has grown weak, for the Lord has put pains into my hands; I shall not be able to stand.
verses.1:15: Samekh. The Lord has removed all my mighty ones from my midst; He has summoned an appointed time against me to crush my chosen ones. The Lord has trodden the winepress for the virgin daughter of Judah; for these things I weep.
verses.1:16: Ayin. My eye has poured down water, because he who comforts me, who restores my soul, is far removed from me; my sons have become desolate, because the enemy has prevailed.
verses.1:17: Pe. Zion has spread out her hands; there is none who comforts her. The Lord has given command concerning Jacob: his oppressors are all around him; Jerusalem has become like an unclean woman in their midst.
verses.1:18: Tsade. The Lord is righteous, for I have provoked His mouth. Hear now, all peoples, and behold my sorrow: my virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.
verses.1:19: Qoph. I called to my lovers, but they deceived me; my priests and my elders perished in the city, for they sought food for themselves that they might restore their souls, and they did not find it.
verses.1:20: Resh. Behold, O Lord, for I am afflicted; my inward parts are troubled, and my heart is overturned within me, for in provoking I have been sorely embittered. Outdoors the sword has bereaved of children, just as death within the house.
verses.1:21: Shin. Hear now that I groan; there is none who comforts me. All my enemies have heard of my calamities and have rejoiced, because You have done it. You have brought on the day; You have summoned the appointed time; they have become like me.
verses.1:22: Tav. May all their wickedness come before Your face, and glean them bare in the manner that they made a gleaning because of all my sins; for my groanings are many, and my heart is grieved.
verses.2:1: Aleph. How the Lord in His anger has shrouded the daughter of Zion in darkness! He has cast down from heaven to the earth the glory of Israel, and did not remember the footstool of His feet.
verses.2:2: Beth. In the day of His anger the Lord has engulfed without sparing; He has torn down in His wrath all the beautiful things of Jacob. He has pressed the strongholds of the daughter of Judah to the ground; He has profaned her kings and her princes.
verses.2:3: Gimel. In the wrath of His anger He has called together every horn of Israel; He has drawn back His right hand from before the face of the enemy, and He has kindled a flame like fire in Jacob, and it has devoured all things round about.
verses.2:4: Daleth. He has bent His bow like an opposing enemy; He has steadied His right hand like an adversary, and He has slain all the desirable things of my eyes in the tent of the daughter of Zion; He has poured out His wrath like fire.
verses.2:5: He. The Lord has become like an enemy; He has engulfed Israel. He has engulfed her palaces; He has destroyed his strongholds, and for the daughter of Judah He has multiplied her being humbled and brought low.
verses.2:6: Vav. And He has spread apart His tabernacle like a vine; He has destroyed His feast. The Lord has forgotten what He made in Zion of feast and Sabbath, and in the indignation of His anger He has provoked king and priest and prince.
verses.2:7: Zayin. The Lord has cast off His altar; He has shaken off His sanctuary; He has shattered with His hand the wall of her palaces. They lifted up a voice in the house as on a feast day.
verses.2:8: Heth. And He turned to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; He stretched out a measure; He did not turn back His hand from trampling down. And the rampart mourned, and the wall languished together with it.
verses.2:9: Teth. Her gates have sunk into the earth; He has destroyed and shattered her bars, and her king and her princes among the nations. There is no law; indeed, her prophets also did not see a vision from the Lord.
verses.2:10: Yod. The elders of the daughter of Zion sat upon the ground and kept silent; they cast dust upon their heads; they girded themselves with sackcloth; they brought down to the earth the chief virgins in Jerusalem.
verses.2:11: Kaph. My eyes have failed with tears; my heart is troubled; my glory is poured out upon the earth because of the shattering of the daughter of my people, as infant and nursing child faint in the streets of the city.
verses.2:12: Lamed. To their mothers they said, "Where are grain and wine?" as they fainted like wounded men in the streets of the city, as their souls were poured out into the bosom of their mothers.
verses.2:13: Mem. What shall I testify to you, or to what shall I liken you, O daughter of Jerusalem? Who shall save and comfort you, O virgin daughter of Zion? For the cup of your shattering has been magnified; who shall heal you?
verses.2:14: Nun. Your prophets have seen for you vain things and folly, and they have not uncovered your iniquity so as to turn back your captivity; rather, they have seen for you vain oracles and expulsions.
verses.2:15: Samekh. All who pass by the way have clapped their hands at you; they have hissed and wagged their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "This is the city," they shall say, "the crown of gladness of all the earth."
verses.2:16: Ayin. All your enemies have opened their mouths wide against you; they have hissed and gnashed their teeth, and said, "We have swallowed her up! Surely this is the day for which we waited; we have found it, we have seen it."
verses.2:17: Pe. The Lord has done what He purposed; He has fulfilled His words which He commanded from the days of old. He has torn down and has not spared; and He has caused the enemy to rejoice over you; He has exalted the horn of him who afflicts you.
verses.2:18: Tsade. Their heart cried out to the Lord. O walls of Zion, pour down tears like torrents day and night; give yourself no respite; do not let your eye keep silent, O daughter.
verses.2:19: Qoph. Arise, exult in the night at the beginnings of your watch; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands to Him for the life of the infants who faint with hunger at the head of all the ways out.
verses.2:20: Resh. Behold, O Lord, and consider whom You have gleaned thus! Shall women eat the fruit of their womb? The butcher has made a gleaning! Shall infants nursing at the breasts be slain? Will You kill priest and prophet in the sanctuary of the Lord?
verses.2:21: Shin. Young boy and old man lay down in the street; my virgins and my young men have gone into captivity. By sword and by famine You have slain; in the day of Your anger You butchered; You did not spare.
verses.2:22: Tav. He has summoned as a feast day my sojournings round about, and in the day of the anger of the Lord there was neither one escaping nor one left remaining, as I strengthened and multiplied all my enemies.
verses.3:1: Aleph. I am the man who sees poverty by the rod of His wrath upon me.
verses.3:2: He took me and led me away into darkness, and not light.
verses.3:3: Surely against me He turned His hand all the day.
verses.3:4: He made my flesh and my skin grow old; He shattered my bones.
verses.3:5: Beth. He built up against me, and surrounded my head, and labored.
verses.3:6: In dark places He seated me, like the dead of old.
verses.3:7: He built up against me, and I shall not go out; He made my bronze heavy.
verses.3:8: Gimel. Indeed, though I cry out and call aloud, He has blocked up my prayer.
verses.3:9: Daleth. He walled up my ways; He blocked my paths; He threw them into confusion.
verses.3:10: A bear lying in wait, He is to me a lion in secret places.
verses.3:11: He pursued one who had turned aside and brought me to a halt; He made me desolate.
verses.3:12: He. He stretched His bow and stationed me as a mark for an arrow;
verses.3:13: He drove into my kidneys the arrows of His quiver.
verses.3:14: I became a laughingstock to all my people, their song all the day.
verses.3:15: Vav. He sated me with bitterness; He made me drunk with gall.
verses.3:16: And He knocked out my teeth with gravel; He fed me ashes.
verses.3:17: And He cast away my soul from peace; I forgot good things.
verses.3:18: And my victory perished, and my hope from the Lord.
verses.3:19: Zayin. I remembered from my poverty and from persecution; my bitterness and gall shall be remembered,
verses.3:20: and my soul shall brood over me.
verses.3:21: This I shall set in my heart; therefore I shall wait patiently.
verses.3:25: Heth. Good is the Lord to those who wait for Him, to the soul that shall seek Him who is good.
verses.3:26: And he shall wait and be still for the salvation of the Lord.
verses.3:27: Teth. It is good for a man when he takes up a yoke in his youth;
verses.3:28: he shall sit alone and keep silent, because he has taken it upon himself.
verses.3:30: Yod. He shall give his cheek to the one who strikes him; he shall be sated with reproaches,
verses.3:31: for the Lord will not reject forever.
verses.3:32: Kaph. For the One who has humbled will show compassion, even according to the multitude of His mercy;
verses.3:33: He did not answer from His heart and humble the sons of man.
verses.3:34: Lamed. To humble under his feet all the prisoners of the earth,
verses.3:35: to turn aside the judgment of a man before the face of the Most High,
verses.3:36: to condemn a man when he is judged—the Lord has not spoken.
verses.3:37: Who spoke thus, and it came to pass? The Lord did not command it.
verses.3:38: Out of the mouth of the Most High, shall not evil things and good come forth?
verses.3:39: Mem. Why should a living mortal murmur, a man concerning his sin?
verses.3:40: Nun. Our way has been searched out and examined; and let us turn back even to the Lord;
verses.3:41: let us lift up our hearts upon our hands to the High One in heaven:
verses.3:42: We have sinned, we have acted ungodly, and You have not forgiven.
verses.3:43: Samekh. You covered over in wrath and drove us away; You slew, You did not spare.
verses.3:44: You covered Yourself with a cloud on account of prayer,
verses.3:45: that I should close my eyes and be cast away. Ayin. You set us in the midst of the peoples;
verses.3:46: all our enemies opened wide their mouth against us.
verses.3:47: Fear and wrath have come upon us, lifting up and crushing.
verses.3:48: My eye shall pour down streams of waters over the shattering of the daughter of my people.
verses.3:49: Pe. My eye has been swallowed up, and I shall not keep silent, because there is no respite,
verses.3:50: until the Lord looks down from heaven and beholds.
verses.3:51: My eye shall glean upon my soul above all the daughters of the city.
verses.3:52: Tsade. Hunting, they hunted me like a sparrow—all my enemies without cause;
verses.3:53: they put my life to death in a pit and laid a stone upon me;
verses.3:54: water overflowed upon my head; I said, "I have been cast away."
verses.3:55: Qoph. I called upon Your name, O Lord, out of the deepest pit;
verses.3:56: You heard my voice; do not hide Your ears to my supplication.
verses.3:57: To my help You drew near; on the day that I called upon You, You said to me, "Do not fear."
verses.3:58: Resh. You judged, O Lord, the causes of my soul; You redeemed my life.
verses.3:59: You saw, O Lord, my troubles; You judged my cause.
verses.3:60: You saw all their vengeance, even into all their devices against me.
verses.3:61: Shin. You heard their reproach, all their devices against me,
verses.3:62: the lips of those who rise up against me and their meditations against me all the day,
verses.3:63: their sitting down and their rising up. Look upon their eyes;
verses.3:64: You shall render to them a recompense, O Lord, according to the works of their hands.
verses.3:65: Tav. You shall render to them a shielding, a toil of heart.
verses.3:66: You shall pursue them in anger and utterly consume them from beneath heaven, O Lord.
verses.4:1: Aleph. How shall gold be dimmed, and the good silver be changed? Holy stones have been poured out at the head of all the streets.
verses.4:2: Beth. The precious sons of Zion, who were exalted in gold—how have they been reckoned as earthen vessels, the works of a potter's hands?
verses.4:3: Gimel. Even dragons have bared their breasts; their whelps have nursed upon the daughters of my people to an incurable state, like a sparrow in a wilderness.
verses.4:4: Daleth. The tongue of the nursing infant clung to his throat in thirst; little children asked for bread, yet there is no one breaking it for them.
verses.4:5: He. Those who ate the provisions have vanished in the streets; those who were brought up upon scarlet have clothed themselves with dunghills.
verses.4:6: Vav. And the iniquity of the daughter of my people was made greater than the iniquities of Sodom, which was overthrown as in haste, and they did not labor with their hands in her.
verses.4:7: Zayin. Her Nazirites were purer than snow; they shone brighter than milk; they glowed more fiery than stones; their cutting was of sapphire.
verses.4:8: Heth. Their appearance has grown darker than soot; they were not recognized in the streets; their skin clung fast upon their bones; they were dried up; they became like wood.
verses.4:9: Teth. Better were the slain of the sword than the slain of famine; they departed, pierced through, from the produce of the fields.
verses.4:10: Yod. The hands of compassionate women boiled their own children; they became food for them in the crushing of the daughter of my people.
verses.4:11: Kaph. The Lord has accomplished His fury; He has poured out the fierceness of His wrath, and kindled a fire in Zion, and it devoured her foundations.
verses.4:12: Lamed. The kings of the earth, all who dwell in the inhabited world, did not believe that an enemy and oppressor would enter through the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.4:13: Mem. Because of the sins of her prophets, the injustices of her priests, who shed righteous blood in her midst.
verses.4:14: Nun. Her watchers staggered in the streets; they were defiled with blood; in their inability, they touched their garments.
verses.4:15: Samekh. Depart from the unclean; call to them, "Depart, depart, do not touch!" For they were kindled, and indeed they staggered; say among the nations, "They shall no longer sojourn."
verses.4:16: Ayin. The face of the Lord is their portion; He will no longer look upon them. They did not regard the face of the priests; they had no mercy on the prophets.
verses.4:17: Pe. While we still existed, our eyes failed, as we watched in vain for our help.
verses.4:18: Tsade. We watched for a nation that does not save; we hunted our little ones, so as not to walk in our squares.
verses.4:19: Qoph. Our time has drawn near, our days have been fulfilled, our time has arrived. Those who pursue us became swifter than the eagles of heaven; upon the mountains they flew forth; in the wilderness they lay in wait for us.
verses.4:20: Resh. The breath of our countenance, the anointed Lord, was captured in their corruptions—of whom we said, "In His shadow we shall live among the nations."
verses.4:21: Shin. Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Idumea, who dwells upon the earth; even to you the cup of the Lord shall pass; you shall become drunk and pour yourself out.
verses.4:22: Tav. Your iniquity has come to an end, O daughter of Zion; He will no longer carry you away into exile. He has visited your iniquities, O daughter of Edom; He has uncovered your impieties.
verses.5:1: Remember, O Lord, what has come upon us; look down and behold our reproach.
verses.5:2: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
verses.5:3: We have become orphans; there is no father; our mothers are like widows.
verses.5:4: From our days, our wood came in exchange; upon our neck
verses.5:5: we were pursued; we toiled, and we were given no rest.
verses.5:6: Egypt gave a hand, Assyria to their fill.
verses.5:7: Our fathers sinned, and they are no more; we have borne their iniquities.
verses.5:8: Servants have ruled over us; there is no one who redeems from their hand.
verses.5:9: At the peril of our lives we shall bring in our bread, because of the sword of the wilderness.
verses.5:10: Our skin has grown livid like an oven; they were shriveled up because of the tempests of famine.
verses.5:11: They humbled women in Zion, virgins in the cities of Judah.
verses.5:12: Rulers were hanged by their hands; elders were not honored.
verses.5:13: Chosen men took up weeping, and young men grew weak under wood.
verses.5:14: And aged men have ceased from the gate; chosen men have ceased from their psalms.
verses.5:15: The joy of our heart has ceased; our dance has been turned into mourning.
verses.5:16: The crown of our head has fallen. Woe indeed to us, for we have sinned!
verses.5:17: Because of this our heart has become a grievous sorrow; because of this our eyes have grown dark.
verses.5:18: Because of Mount Zion, for it has been laid desolate, foxes have passed through it.
verses.5:19: Yet You, O Lord, shall dwell forever; Your throne endures from generation to generation.
verses.5:20: Why will You utterly forget us? Will You forsake us for length of days?
verses.5:21: Turn us back, O Lord, to You, and we shall be turned back; and renew our days as before.
verses.5:22: For You have utterly rejected us; You have been exceedingly angry against us.

notes.1:1: The Greek opens with a prose superscription attributing the lament to Jeremiah after Israel's captivity and Jerusalem's desolation, and retains the Hebrew acrostic letter names (Aleph through Tav) at the start of each verse.
notes.1:7: The Greek reads "at her habitation" (katoikesia), reflecting a reading of the underlying Hebrew from the root "to dwell" rather than "her downfall."
notes.1:12: The opening "To you, all who pass by the way" follows the Greek literal rendering (hoi pros hymas), and the following clause reads "having spoken against me" (phthengxamenos en emoi).
notes.1:14: The Greek reads "Watch was kept" (egregorethe), "in my hands they were intertwined," and "has put pains into my hands," diverging markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:22: The Greek employs the vine-gleaning metaphor ("glean them bare" and third-person plural "they made a gleaning"), an idiom that recurs in 2:20.
notes.2:3: The Greek text here reads synekalesen ("called together") rather than syneklasen ("broke in pieces").
notes.2:10: The Greek reads "brought down to the earth the chief virgins" (archegous parthenous), rendering the Hebrew word for "their head" as "leaders/chief ones" modifying the virgins.
notes.2:19: The Greek verb agalliasai ("exult") literally renders a Hebrew verb for crying aloud that commonly denotes joyful shouting.
notes.2:20: The Greek reads "The butcher [mageiros, literally 'cook/butcher'] has made a gleaning," continuing the vine-gleaning metaphor of 1:22 and linking lexically with "You butchered" (emageireusas) in 2:21.
notes.2:22: The Greek opens in the third person ("He has summoned") with "my sojournings" (paroikias mou) and closes with "as I strengthened and multiplied all my enemies," differing substantially from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.3:1: The Greek text preserves the Hebrew acrostic letter names in Greek transcription (e.g., Aleph, Be, Zai, Labd), rendered here with their standard English spellings; it also reads "poverty" (ptocheian) and attaches "upon me" to the end of verse 1.
notes.3:5: The Septuagint reads "my head, and labored" (kephalen mou kai emochthesen), taking the Hebrew word for "gall/poison" as its homonym "head" and rendering "hardship" as a verb.
notes.3:25: The Greek text omits verses 22–24, places the Heth acrostic heading here, and concludes verse 25 with "good" (agathon), which in the Hebrew opens verse 26.
notes.3:30: The Greek text omits verse 29; in verse 28 it also reads reflexively "he has taken it upon himself" (eph' heauto).
notes.3:33: The Septuagint reads "He did not answer" (ouk apekrithe), translating the Hebrew root as "to answer" rather than its homonym "to afflict."
notes.3:40: The Septuagint uses passive verbs ("has been searched out and examined") with singular "our way," rather than the Hebrew cohortatives ("let us search and examine our ways").
notes.3:45: The Greek attaches "that I should close my eyes and be cast away" (kammysai me kai aposthenai) to verse 44 and places the Ayin acrostic heading mid-verse, differing markedly from the Hebrew ("refuse and rubbish").
notes.3:63: The Septuagint reads "Look upon their eyes" (epiblepson ep' ophthalmous auton), whereas the Hebrew has "Look! I am their taunting song."
notes.3:65: The Greek reads "a shielding, a toil of heart" (hyperaspismon, kardias mochthon), rendering the Hebrew for "obstinacy of heart" literally as a shield-covering and reading "Your curse" as "toil."
notes.4:1: The Greek preserves the Hebrew acrostic letter headings (with distinctive Greek spellings such as Be, Labd, Tiade, Rechs, and Chsen), rendered here with standard English letter names. The Greek also reads "the good silver" (to argyrion to agathon) where the Hebrew reads fine gold.
notes.4:3: The Greek presents distinctive vocabulary and syntax here: drakontes ("dragons"), strouthion ("sparrow"), and nominative skymnoi ("their whelps") paired with accusative thygateras ("daughters of my people").
notes.4:14: The Greek reads egregoroi ("watchers") where the Hebrew has "blind," and uses the finite verb hepsanto ("they touched") after "in their inability."
notes.4:18: The Greek begins verse 18 with "We watched for a nation that does not save" (shifting the verse boundary with 4:19 relative to the Hebrew) and reads "we hunted our little ones" (mikrous) rather than "they hunted our steps."
notes.4:20: The Greek reads the nominative christos Kyrios ("the anointed Lord" or "Christ the Lord"), differing from the Hebrew genitive "the anointed of the Lord," and renders the Hebrew "pits" as diaphthorais ("corruptions"). In 4:21-22 the Greek likewise distinguishes "Idumea" (4:21) from "Edom" (4:22).
notes.5:4: Following Codex Vaticanus, the Greek reads "From our days" (omitting the Hebrew clause about drinking water for money) and breaks the clause across verses 4 and 5 ("upon our neck / we were pursued").
notes.5:6: The Greek places "Egypt" in the nominative as the subject of the singular verb "gave a hand," and omits "bread" after "to their fill."
notes.5:13: The Greek reads "Chosen men took up weeping" (klauthmon), where the Hebrew refers to young men carrying the millstone.
